name: Impacket - NTLM Relay to ADCS (ESC8)
description: ESC8 relays a coerced NTLM authentication to the ADCS web-enrollment endpoint to obtain a certificate for the victim account. Combine with a coercion trigger (printerbug) to force a Domain Controller to authenticate to the relay.

examples.label: Relay to ADCS for a cert (ESC8)

notes:
Relay coerced NTLM auth to AD CS web enrollment (ESC8) to obtain a cert for a privileged account, then PKINIT to a TGT - a classic domain-takeover chain.
Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 19 (Password Attacks)

recommended.note: Turn the certificate into a usable TGT.

defense.why_it_works: ntlmrelayx relays a coerced NTLM authentication to the ADCS web-enrollment endpoint (ESC8) to obtain a certificate for the victim identity (e.g. a DC), then uses it via PKINIT.
defense.prerequisites: ADCS web enrollment over HTTP (no EPA), a coercion vector, and a relay host.
defense.impact: A certificate for a privileged identity (often a DC) enabling PKINIT auth and DCSync - domain compromise.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1649] Certificate-based Kerberos auth (PKINIT): 4768 with a certificate; on the CA, 4886/4887 certificate requests where the SAN != requester; abnormal certificate issuance; ntlmrelay to ADCS shows a relayed request from a non-DC IP. On the CA, a DomainController-template request sourced from the relay IP rather than the DC.
defense.artifacts: A relayed cert request (4886/4887 from the relay IP); the issued cert; coercion + relay traffic.
defense.prevention: Enforce HTTPS + Extended Protection for Authentication on ADCS web enrollment; disable it if unused; block coercion (patch/disable Spooler); Harden ADCS templates (remove ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT, require manager approval, restrict enrollment); enforce HTTPS + Extended Protection on web enrollment (ESC8); monitor 4886/4887 and PKINIT logons; restrict who can enroll.
defense.evasion: The certificate persists for years and is usable offline from any host, decoupling exploitation from the noisy relay step.
defense.misconfiguration: Pass-the-Certificate (PtC) attacks exploit ADCS certificate abuse (ESC1/ESC8) combined with Kerberos PKINIT. Shadow credentials (pywhisker) exploit write access to msDS-KeyCredentialLink to add a certificate-based authentication mechanism to any account. Pass-the-Ticket works because Kerberos tickets are extractable from LSASS memory.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# msDS-KeyCredentialLink writable by attacker (GenericWrite on target account):
# pywhisker.py -t targetuser -a add
# Adds a fake device credential -> obtain certificate for targetuser
# -> PKINIT TGT as targetuser -> NTLM hash via UnPAC

# LSASS memory contains TGTs for all logged-in users:
# Mimikatz: sekurlsa::tickets /export
# Rubeus: dump /all
defense.secure_config:
# Prevent msDS-KeyCredentialLink abuse:
# Audit who has GenericWrite on privileged accounts
# Only SYSTEM/DCs should write msDS-KeyCredentialLink
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity admin -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'Write'}

# Prevent ticket extraction:
# Enable Credential Guard (blocks LSASS memory reads)
# Protected Users group members: tickets not cached in LSASS

# ADCS: prevent ESC1/ESC8 (see those cards)
# Monitor: Event 4768 with certificate auth, Event 4769 unusual ticket lifetimes

steps.label: Use the issued cert for a TGT
